ratios.name: Gold / Silver
ratios.read: An ounce of gold buys 72 ounces of silver, the 50th percentile of the past 20 years and rising over 3 months. Neither haven demand nor industrial demand dominates.

ratios.name: Copper / Gold
ratios.read: Copper relative to gold is at the 14th percentile of 20 years and rising over 3 months. Safety is being priced ahead of growth.

ratios.name: Gold / Oil
ratios.pair: barrels of WTI per oz gold
ratios.read: An ounce of gold buys 42.0 barrels of WTI, the 88th percentile of 20 years and falling over 3 months. Gold is expensive against oil, typical of haven demand or weak energy demand.

ratios.name: Oil / Natural gas
ratios.read: A barrel of WTI costs 29.9 times an MMBtu of Henry Hub gas (energy parity is about 5.8), the 81st percentile of 10 years. US gas is cheap relative to crude, which supports gas-fired power and LNG export margins.

ratios.name: Brent vs WTI
ratios.read: Brent trades at a 2.8% premium to WTI, the 12th percentile of 10 years. A narrow spread points to a tight US market or strong US export demand.

ratios.name: 3-2-1 crack spread
ratios.pair: refining margin as % of crude cost
ratios.read: Refined products in New York Harbor are worth 39% more than the crude they're made from (3-2-1 crack), the 74th percentile of 10 years. Refining margins are in their normal range.

ratios.name: Soybeans / Corn
ratios.read: Soybeans are priced at 2.44 times corn per bushel (47th percentile of 20 years). Neither crop has a clear planting advantage.

ratios.name: S&P 500 / Gold
ratios.read: The S&P 500 priced in gold is at the 22nd percentile of 10 years and roughly flat over 3 months. Equities and gold are in their usual relationship.

ratios.name: S&P 500 / Oil
ratios.read: The S&P 500 priced in barrels of WTI is at the 84th percentile of 10 years and falling over 3 months. Financial assets are expensive against energy.

links.label: Oil and inflation expectations
links.read: Oil is driving inflation expectations: moves in crude are passing through to breakevens.

links.label: Oil and the dollar
links.read: Oil and the dollar are rising together, a sign that supply, not the currency, is setting the oil price.

links.label: Equities and bond yields
links.read: Equities are not reacting consistently to yield moves.

links.label: Oil and equities
links.read: Oil and equities are moving in opposite directions, typical of a supply shock.

read.line: Ratios lean toward growth: industrial metals and equities are gaining on gold.
notes: Gold / Oil is at the 88th percentile (growth fears).
Brent vs WTI is at the 12th percentile (us tightness).
Copper / Gold is at the 14th percentile (growth scare).
